definition: Setting: G = Z_p acts faithfully, orientation-preservingly on W = O x R^{d-n} (O a connected invariant chart subset of R^n, d odd >= 3, d > n). c: S^d -> W^+ collapses S^d \ W to infinity, q: W^+ -> Y = W^+/G, and t: Y -> X is a 'compact test' (X a compact test space, b_t = t(q(infinity)) with a basis of contractible neighbourhoods). Put f_t = t q c, A_t = R f_{t*} C_{S^d} (C = R^2 with B(z,w) = Re(z wbar)), alpha_t: A_t -> D_{X,d} A_t the pushed-forward orientation form; [A_t, alpha_t] lies in E_d(X) = W_d(T(X)), the triangular Witt group of the test category T(X) (thick subcategory of D^b(Sh_R(X)) generated by Rf_* R_B for arbitrary continuous f from compact polyhedra B). Off b_t, A_t is the pushforward of the orbit sheaf H = q_* C, which splits by characters Lambda = mu_{p^infty}: H = (+)_lambda H_lambda, H_lambda = ker(T - M_lambda). A finite partition Lambda = D_0 u ... u D_{m-1} gives projectors that are orthogonal and self-adjoint on A_t|_{X \ b_t} (Lemma orthogonality), hence, via the germ theorem, endomorphisms e_i of A_t in the Verdier quotient Q_U(X) = T(X)/T(U) for a contractible open U containing b_t, with e_i e_j = delta_ij e_i, sum e_i = 1, e_i^dagger = e_i. DEFINITION (06-character-classes.tex:225-235): z_i(t) in E_d(X) is the unique class with  l_U(z_i(t)) = [A_t, alpha_t] + [A_t, alpha_t o (2 e_i - id)]  in W_d(Q_U(X)), where l_U: E_d(X) -> W_d(Q_U(X)) is the integral localization isomorphism (valid because U is contractible and d is odd). No image object of e_i is formed; if e_i did split orthogonally, the right side would be 2 times the Witt class of the e_i-summand. Proved properties: independent of U; sum_i z_i(t) = 2 [A_t, alpha_t] integrally (explicit isometry S = sum_j E_j P_j, S^2 = 1, S^dagger Q_0 S = Q); covariant g_* z_i(t) = z_i(g t); homotopy invariant in t (close-pair space C_d); and for a test h concentrated on a region V of p^k labelled sheets, multiplication by the sheet multiplier beta conjugates e_i to e_{i-1}, so z_0(h) = ... = z_{m-1}(h). Used with I49: fix the lattice L_d^{-1} Z u_d first, then for m = p^k > 4 L_d the m integral classes z_i(a) have equal rational images summing to 4 u_d, so each is (4/m) u_d, outside the lattice.
obstruction_dissolved: A faithful Z_p-action should be ruled out by a 'Haar fraction' argument: the action spreads a degree-one class equally over p^k character parts for every k, so each part carries 1/p^k of it. Classically this needs an integer-valued invariant for each part, and three things block it. (1) Wild orbit spaces. Y = W/G has cohomological dimension n+2 (Yang) and non-finitely-generated cohomology, so Euler-characteristic, transfer or Smith-theory counts on Y give no integers. (2) Splitting needs dividing. Isotypic decompositions split ordinary (co)homology only after inverting |G| (here infinite) or tensoring with C. Complex-coefficient homology loses integrality: the character parts of H_*(.;C) are just vector spaces, with no lattice to violate. (3) The bad point. The character decomposition of the orbit sheaf exists only away from b = t(y_inf), the image of the point at infinity and of the non-free orbits collapsed there. The projectors do not extend to direct summands of A_t over b, and the stalks are infinite-dimensional, so one cannot form 'the e_i-part' as an object of a category with a Witt group. The device dissolves all three. Real coefficients plus Witt groups give integrality, since signatures are integers and Witt classes are integral before tensoring with Q. The 'twice the summand' form [A, alpha] + [A, alpha(2e-1)] needs only a self-adjoint idempotent on the existing object, not its image. Defining it in the Verdier quotient by a contractible neighbourhood of b, and lifting through the integral localization isomorphism (odd d), removes the bad point. The result is an integral, natural, homotopy-invariant class for each part of an infinite (profinite) character decomposition. Without it, the fixed-lattice contradiction of I49 has nothing integral to apply to.
abstract_mechanism: Given a self-dual object whose symmetry splits it into many parts only generically (off a small 'bad' locus), assign each part an integral class without ever splitting off the part. Take the form plus the same form twisted by the reflection 2e-1, which equals twice the part's class. Then lift it from the localized category (bad locus killed) back to the global integral group, using an isomorphism that holds because the bad locus is contractible. The parts sum to a fixed integral total and a cyclic symmetry permutes them, so each part equals total/m. With denominators bounded a priori by a lattice fixed before m, m = p^k large gives a contradiction. In short: integral 'isotypic signatures' for a profinite symmetry, defined by reflection-twisting and localization-lifting, defeat the fractional Haar measure of the parts.

candidates.problem: Generalized Hilbert–Smith conjecture for (ENR / ANR) Z-homology manifolds (equivalently: Z_p admits no effective action on a connected finite-dimensional homology or cohomology manifold over Z).
candidates.reference: Bredon, Introduction to Compact Transformation Groups (1972), Ch. on Smith theory, and Borel et al., Seminar on Transformation Groups (1960): Yang's theorem dim_Z(X/Z_p) = n+2 is proved for homology manifolds. Dranishnikov, 'On some problems related to the Hilbert–Smith conjecture', arXiv:1504.07277. Mj, arXiv:0906.4243 (Thm 2.24 is a metric version on Z_p-cohomology manifolds).
candidates.status: Open (no proof found in any dimension >= 3 for general homology manifolds; the manifold case is the 304 claim). Caveat: Mj (0906.4243, p. 3-4) writes that the analogue of his Thm 2.24 is false for purely topological actions on homology manifolds, citing Raymond–Williams 1963. But the Raymond–Williams/Levin spaces are 2-dimensional inverse-limit compacta (arXiv:1909.12660), not visibly homology manifolds. The remark seems to concern general metric compacta and needs checking before investing.
candidates.obstruction_match: Exact. Yang's theorem shows the obstruction (wild orbit space of dimension n+2) is identical for homology manifolds. Each manifold-specific input of the 304 proof has a homology-manifold analogue: (a) Newman's theorem holds for Z/p-cohomology manifolds via Smith theory (Bredon). (b) Verdier duality with orientation sheaf, all the character-class construction needs off b. (c) A_t lies in T(X): for a compact ENR source N, a retraction N -> P -> N through a finite polyhedron makes Rf_*R_N a direct summand of R(f r)_* R_P, and T is closed under summands. The paper's choice to generate T by arbitrary continuous maps and close under summands is exactly what permits this.
candidates.adaptation_sketch: Keep the lattice step on S^d unchanged (it only concerns S^d). Replace the collapse c: S^d -> W^+ (which needs W open in R^d) by a compact ENR source N -> W^+ that is a homeomorphism over a neighbourhood of the support of the test. For example, a compact ENR homology-manifold neighbourhood of the pinch region, collapsing its boundary to infinity; the form then needs nonsingularity only in the quotient Q_U(X), where boundary effects sit over b. Replace the pinch by a degree-one map W^+ -> S^d from Hopf's theorem for d-dimensional compacta. Average it over a small subgroup exactly as in Lemma averaged-test. Then run z_i, equal parts and the lattice as written. The steps to check are the identity [A_a, alpha_a] = 2 (aqc)_* u_d with a homology-manifold source (rationally E_d(S^d) = Q, detected by H_d, so it should hold) and the rational-transfer / odd-sphere telescope (no manifold input).
candidates.expected_payoff: Resolves (would settle the generalized Hilbert–Smith conjecture for ENR homology manifolds, including Bryant–Ferry–Mio–Weinberger exotic homology manifolds).
candidates.confidence: low-medium (the device ports cleanly; the global source replacement and the Mj caveat are the risks)

candidates.problem: Remove the Hausdorff/conformal-dimension hypothesis in Mj's theorem: a group Q of boundary values of quasi-isometries of a Poincaré-duality hyperbolic group G cannot contain Z_p, hence finite-dimensional locally compact such Q are Lie. Mj assumes dim_Haus(∂G, d) < dim_t + 2 for some visual metric (equivalently ACD(∂G) < dim_t + 2). The same hypothesis feeds his pattern-rigidity theorems.
candidates.reference: M. Mj, 'Pattern rigidity and the Hilbert–Smith conjecture', Geom. Topol. 16 (2012), arXiv:0906.4243, Thm 2.24, Cor 2.25; answers a question of Iwaniec–Martin (Remark 2, p. 527 of [IM01]).
candidates.status: Open without the dimension hypothesis (as of the sources found).
candidates.obstruction_match: Same p-adic exclusion on a non-manifold space: ∂G for a PD(n) hyperbolic group is a Z-homology (n-1)-manifold (Bestvina 1996). Mj's proof is the Repovš–Ščepin / Martin Hausdorff-dimension count, which is why he needs dim_Haus < dim_t + 2. The character-class argument uses no metric, so if C1 holds the hypothesis disappears.
candidates.adaptation_sketch: Apply C1 to X = ∂G with the topological Z_p-action (quasi-isometries act by homeomorphisms). If ∂G is an ENR (open in general; true for many PD boundaries), C1's summand trick applies directly. Otherwise one needs T-categories generated by maps from compact ENR homology manifolds, or a Čech-approximation argument. When ∂G is a sphere (e.g. S^2, Cannon setting; release family 246), the manifold theorem of 304 already applies, with no adaptation.
candidates.expected_payoff: Resolves (Mj Cor 2.25 and the pattern-rigidity consequences without dimension hypotheses), conditional on C1.
candidates.difficulty: high (inherits C1 plus ANR questions for boundaries)

candidates.problem: Local Hilbert–Smith: a local action (pseudogroup / germs) of a neighbourhood of 0 in Z_p, by local homeomorphisms of R^n, faithful on germs at a point, is impossible. This is the HS analogue of the local Hilbert fifth problem (Jacoby; Goldbring 2010, 'Hilbert's fifth problem for local groups', Annals).
candidates.reference: I. Goldbring, Hilbert's fifth problem for local groups, Ann. of Math. 172 (2010). Pardon 2013 §4.1 chart reduction (already localizes the global problem).
candidates.status: Not stated as a named open problem in the sources found; folklore-adjacent. Status unverified.
candidates.obstruction_match: Strong structurally. The whole 304 machine is local: everything happens on one invariant chart subset O, a pinch ball, and a region V of p^k labelled sheets. The z_i classes only see A_t on a compact test target. The global group structure is used only through invariance of O and the existence of small open subgroups, both available for a local action restricted to a sufficiently small open subgroup.
candidates.adaptation_sketch: Given a local Z_p-action near x, a compact open subgroup p^j Z_p acts genuinely on some invariant neighbourhood: take the saturation of a small ball, as in Prop chart-reduction. Then the global proof applies verbatim. If saturation fails for genuinely local actions, run the averaged test and the sheet lemma inside the domain of definition.
candidates.expected_payoff: Resolves (likely a short corollary once 304 is accepted; the device needs no change).
candidates.confidence: medium (that it ports); low (that it is a recognised open problem)

candidates.problem: Weak Hilbert–Smith conjecture: no infinite compact zero-dimensional group acts freely on a manifold with finite-dimensional orbit space. This comes with the Borsuk–Ulam-type BDH conjecture -> Ageev conjecture -> weak HS chain.
candidates.reference: Chirvasitu, Dąbrowski, Tobolski, 'The weak Hilbert–Smith conjecture from a Borsuk–Ulam-type conjecture', arXiv:1612.09567. Dranishnikov arXiv:1504.07277 (reduction to Essential Lens Sequence + Injectivity conjectures, after R. F. Williams' K-theory programme).
candidates.status: Open before Oct 2026; implied by the 304 theorem if correct.
candidates.obstruction_match: Theorem-level only. Weak HS is a special case of HS, so the device is not needed beyond the 304 proof itself. One device-level comparison: Williams/Dranishnikov use K-theory of B Z_p 'infinite products' to defeat the fractional parts, and 304 does it with Witt groups of real sheaves. The two are parallel integrality devices.
candidates.adaptation_sketch: None needed (corollary). Optional: the BDH/Ageev equivariant-map statements for profinite G might be attacked with character classes of G^{*n}. No concrete route found.
candidates.expected_payoff: Resolves as a corollary (not a device transfer).

candidates.problem: Removing the Lie-group hypothesis from results on compact or locally compact group actions on manifolds that are stated only for Lie groups because of Hilbert–Smith. Examples: (a) Conner–Raymond: a compact connected group acting effectively on a closed aspherical manifold is a torus (Lie case classical; general compact case via Gottlieb–Lee–Özaydin-type arguments needs HS). (b) Q. Khan, 'Countable approximation of topological G-manifolds III' (arXiv:1905.09977), restricted to Lie G 'limited by' HS. (c) Topological Zimmer-type statements for non-discrete groups.
candidates.reference: arXiv:1905.09977; Gottlieb–Lee–Özaydin, Trans. AMS 287 (1985); Fisher, arXiv:0809.4849.
candidates.status: Open in the non-Lie case; each becomes a corollary of the 304 theorem.
candidates.obstruction_match: Theorem-level only. These are consequences of HS, not of the character-class device.
candidates.adaptation_sketch: Cite 304 Thm cor:lie; no device adaptation.

candidates.problem: Hilbert–Smith in the symplectic / C^0-Hamiltonian setting, and Polterovich–Shelukhin questions on p-adic actions by Hamiltonian homeomorphisms. Example: drop Shelukhin's asphericity conditions (symplectic class and c_1 vanishing on pi_2).
candidates.reference: E. Shelukhin, 'A symplectic Hilbert–Smith conjecture' (2024), arXiv:2403.07195, Thm A.
candidates.status: Partially solved (Shelukhin under the asphericity hypotheses); the general case follows from 304's theorem, since Hamiltonian homeomorphisms are homeomorphisms.
candidates.obstruction_match: Same statement in a restricted class. Shelukhin's Floer power operations play the role of the integral invariant; z_i replaces them with Witt classes needing no symplectic structure.
candidates.adaptation_sketch: None (direct specialization). Use as a held-out comparison: Floer-theoretic proof vs character-class proof.
candidates.expected_payoff: Simplifies a known proof / removes hypotheses (via the theorem).

candidates.problem: Integral isotypic signatures for p-adic towers of covers. Examples: denominators and rationality of L^2-signatures and Levine–Tristram signatures at mu_{p^infty} for Z_p-towers (Lück–Schick approximation of L^2-signatures; Casson–Gordon prime-power signature invariants).
candidates.reference: W. Lück, T. Schick, Various L^2-signatures and a topological L^2-signature theorem (2003); Borodzik–Conway–Politarczyk, Twisted Blanchfield pairings and twisted signatures I/II, arXiv:2111.10632, arXiv:1809.08791.
candidates.status: Various open questions (e.g. topological invariance/concordance invariance of signature-type invariants at non-prime-power roots). None matches the 304 obstruction exactly.
candidates.obstruction_match: Partial and mostly superficial. The objects (signatures of character parts of a profinite cyclic symmetry) are the same kind, but in tower settings the parts already split, as finite covers with finite-dimensional homology. The two blocks the device removes (non-splitting at a bad point; wild orbit space) are absent.
candidates.adaptation_sketch: One could define z_i-type classes for the Z_p-tower of a knot complement's infinite cyclic cover, with the branch locus as the 'bad point' localized away. No problem was identified where this beats the existing twisted-signature machinery.

candidates.problem: Strong Atiyah conjecture: bounded denominators of L^2-Betti numbers, in the lcm of orders of finite subgroups.
candidates.reference: Lück, L^2-Invariants (2002), Ch. 10; Grigorchuk–Żuk, Austin (irrational L^2-Betti numbers via lamplighter groups).
candidates.status: Open for many classes; false without bounded torsion.
candidates.obstruction_match: Analogy only: 'fractional parts (1/m) vs an a-priori integral lattice' is I49's numerical shape. But Atiyah concerns von Neumann dimensions over discrete groups, and z_i concerns Witt classes of sheaves for compact groups. No mechanism transfers.

candidates.problem: Rokhlin-type K-theoretic obstructions for Z_p / compact-group actions on C*-algebras: Rokhlin projections permuted cyclically and summing to 1 force p-divisibility of [1] in K_0.
candidates.reference: M. Izumi, Finite group actions on C*-algebras with the Rohlin property I (Duke 2004); E. Gardella et al., Compact group actions with the Rokhlin property (arXiv:1802.01462).
candidates.obstruction_match: Same equal-parts mechanism as I49 (cyclic symmetry permutes parts that sum to a fixed integral total). This is a PRECEDENT for the I49 shape, not a downstream target.
candidates.adaptation_sketch: A real/Witt (KO or L-theory) analogue for Rokhlin actions on real C*-algebras would be the closest transfer. No open problem found that needs it.

candidates.problem: Effective / quantitative Newman theorem via the fixed lattice: no faithful action of a cyclic group Z/p^K with p^k > 4 L_d (L_d = 2^{e_d}, e_d = 3(9^d - 1)/4) whose orbits all lie within the pinch scale of a chart ball.
candidates.reference: Newman 1931; Dress 1969 (Newman via Smith theory); Ku–Ku–Mann 1985 (Newman property for compact non-Lie groups).
candidates.url: (no URL; M.H.A. Newman, Quart. J. Math. 2 (1931) 1-8)
candidates.status: Newman-type theorems are known with existential constants.
candidates.obstruction_match: Weak. For finite G the averaged test does give a degree-one test when all orbits are small, so the device yields an explicit Newman-type statement. But Newman's theorem already excludes ANY nontrivial periodic map with all orbits small, so nothing new follows.
candidates.adaptation_sketch: Run Lemma averaged-test with finite H = G, then z_i for single-character parts.

release_reuse: Grepped data/raw/openai-math/CONTENTS.md and all preprint .tex for Hilbert–Smith, Witt group, Balmer–Walter, Verdier, Newman, Smith theory, isotypic and signature. No other family uses character classes, sheaf Witt groups or the equal-parts lattice device. Other hits: 'Witt groups' appears only in passing in family 'Finite Congruence Lattices' (forward_a.tex:887, quadratic-form context, unrelated); Smith theory appears in family 314 (chromatic fixed-point loss, finite p-groups, chromatic homotopy, no Witt/signature device). Adjacent families that could consume the THEOREM (not the device): 246 (Cannon's conjecture; Mj-type QI-group statements on S^2 boundaries follow from HS on S^2), 315 (4-dim Singer conjecture, L^2 side, no link found), 207 (Bass trace / Kaplansky idempotents: integrality of traces of idempotents, only a thematic cousin of the 'integral class of an unsplit idempotent' idea). Within 304 itself the device is used once, for Pardon's Conjecture 1.4 via the headline. No reuse.

speedup_targets.theorem: Witt-group 'twice the summand' identity: for a nondegenerate symmetric bilinear space (V,b) over a field of char != 2 and a b-self-adjoint idempotent e, [V,b] + [V, b(.,(2e-1).)] = 2[eV, b|_{eV}] in W(K). For an orthogonal partition of unity e_0..e_{m-1}, sum_i ([V,b] + [V,b(2e_i-1)]) = 2[V,b] (Prop sum-classes, via S = sum_j E_j P_j).
speedup_targets.reference: data/raw/openai-math/preprints/The-Hilbert-Smith-conjecture-in-every-finite-dimension-September-23-2026/build/sections/06-character-classes.tex:236-291; classical for involutions (Hirzebruch–Zagier, The Atiyah–Singer theorem and elementary number theory, 1974).
speedup_targets.formalizable: Yes. Mathlib has LinearMap.BilinForm, QuadraticForm, isometries and orthogonal decompositions, but (as far as checked) no Witt group W(K). Either define it or state it as an isometry (V,b) ⊥ (V,b(2e-1)) ≅ (eV,b) ⊥ (eV,b) ⊥ hyperbolic.
speedup_targets.current_proof_size: about half a page by hand; an estimated 150-300 Lean lines including a minimal Witt-group definition.
speedup_targets.expected_speedup: Small. This is the algebraic kernel of the device. It is a good unit test for whether a model 'finds' the reflection trick, but it is not a long-proof collapse.

speedup_targets.theorem: Isotypic signature formula for a finite cyclic group of isometries of a real (or Hermitian) form: sign(b|_{V_D}) = (sign b + sign b(2e_D - 1))/2 for a union D of characters, and the sum over a partition equals sign b. This is the finite-group shadow of z_i; the classical route is via the G-signatures sign(g, .) and characters.
speedup_targets.formalizable: Yes (Mathlib has Matrix.IsHermitian, eigenspaces, orthogonal projections; signature via Sylvester inertia is partly available).

speedup_note: Honest assessment: the device lives inside a heavy framework (non-constructible sheaf Witt groups, Balmer–Walter localization, the fixed sphere lattice), so no known theorem gets dramatically shorter. The only cleanly measurable, Lean-formalizable targets are its algebraic kernel (S1, S2). S3-S6 show that one uniform proof replaces several special-case technologies; this is a breadth gain, not a per-theorem length gain.
precedent_check: No earlier EQUIVALENT of the composite device was found, and no post-Oct-6-2026 use or discussion was found. Web searches for Hilbert–Smith + Witt group / signature / L-theory / 2026 / OpenAI returned only the standard literature (McAuley 2001, never accepted; Pardon 2013, 2018; Dranishnikov 2015; Shelukhin 2024; Mj 2012; Levin 2019). Components, however, all have clear precedent: (a) The algebraic identity [V,b] + [V,b o T] = 2[V^{+}] for a self-adjoint involution T = 2e-1 is classical: involution signatures sign(T,M) and the isotypic split sign(V^±) = (sign b ± sign(T,M))/2 (Hirzebruch–Jänich; Atiyah–Singer III; Hirzebruch–Zagier). (b) Isotypic / character-part G-signatures for finite groups (Atiyah–Singer; equivariant Witt groups) are classical. (c) Integral Witt groups of sheaf categories and the localization sequence are Balmer 2000, Balmer–Walter 2002 and Woolf 2008, all cited. (d) The equal-parts-in-a-lattice numerical shape (I49) appears in Smith-theory and transfer divisibility, and in Rokhlin-property K-theory divisibility for finite/compact group actions on C*-algebras (Izumi 2004, Gardella). Williams' K-theory 'infinite product' programme for B Z_p (via Dranishnikov 1504.07277) is the closest earlier attempt to beat the Haar fraction with an integral invariant, in K-theory rather than Witt theory. What appears new is the combination. Projectors exist only as germs in a Verdier quotient by a contractible neighbourhood of the bad point; the class is lifted through an integral localization isomorphism valid for odd d; and the stalks are infinite-dimensional, from a profinite character decomposition. Verdict: no downgrade to N0. A judge could defensibly call it N2 ('profinite, localized version of the classical isotypic Witt class'); N3 rests on the localization-lift step and on the proof being correct. Unless C1 (homology manifolds) or another genuine transfer is achieved, the item's downstream evidence is theorem corollaries rather than device reuse.

top5.target: C1: generalized Hilbert–Smith for ENR Z-homology manifolds
top5.argument: This is the only candidate where the device itself, not just the theorem, does the new work. Yang's theorem shows homology manifolds carry exactly the same wild-orbit-space obstruction. Every ingredient of z_i has a homology-manifold analogue: Verdier duality with orientation sheaf, Newman via Smith theory, and the A_t in T(X) membership via the ENR-retract summand trick, which works precisely because T is generated by arbitrary continuous maps and closed under summands. The open step is replacing the S^d -> W^+ collapse by a compact ENR source and checking the degree-one identity. The caveat is Mj's remark that a topological analogue fails 'on homology manifolds'. The cited Raymond–Williams spaces are 2-dimensional compacta, so the remark probably does not apply, but it must be checked first. A success would be strong evidence for a confirmed eureka step.

top5.target: C2: Mj's QI-group / pattern-rigidity theorems without the Hausdorff-dimension hypothesis
top5.argument: Mj's dim_Haus < dim_t + 2 hypothesis exists only because his integral obstruction is a Hausdorff-dimension count (Repovš–Ščepin/Martin style). Character classes are metric-free, so on boundaries of PD hyperbolic groups (Z-homology manifolds) they would remove it. That would give unconditional Lie-ness of finite-dimensional locally compact QI groups and stronger pattern rigidity. This depends on C1 plus ANR-type regularity of ∂G. For S^2 boundaries (Cannon setting, family 246) the 304 theorem applies directly.

The device is local by construction: one chart, one pinch ball, one sheet region V, a compact test target. So it should port to local actions of Z_p after passing to a compact open subgroup and a saturated neighbourhood. It is cheap and likely correct, but may be a routine corollary rather than a recognised open problem, and that status is unverified.

top5.target: C6: symplectic / C^0-Hamiltonian Hilbert–Smith (Shelukhin) without asphericity
top5.argument: Shelukhin's Floer power operations are the symplectic counterpart of an integral per-character invariant. The 304 character classes give the same exclusion for all homeomorphisms, removing Shelukhin's pi_2 conditions. This is a clean held-out comparison of proof technologies, though the payoff comes from the theorem, not a new device use.
